overview: Human echinococcosis is a zoonotic disease caused by parasites, namely tapeworms of the genus Echinococcus. It occurs in 4 forms: cystic echinococcosis, alveolar echinococcosis, polycystic echinococcosis, and unicystic echinococcosis.
treatment: percutaneous treatment of the hydatid cysts with the PAIR (Puncture, Aspiration, Injection, Re-aspiration) technique
transmission: ingesting the parasite eggs in contaminated food and water
consumption of viscera of intermediate hosts that contain the parasite larvae
prevention: avoiding contact with contaminated food and water
complications: progressive and fatal if left untreated
key_facts: cystic echinococcosis is globally distributed and found in every continent except Antarctica
alveolar echinococcosis is confined to the northern hemisphere
human incidence rates for cystic echinococcosis can reach more than 50 per 100 000 person-years
prevalence levels as high as 5%–10% may occur in parts of Argentina, Peru, East Africa, Central Asia and China
